task.title: Persist due recurrence pages atomically
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/907 by persisting one bounded exact-recurrence due page as an all-or-nothing provenance unit.
acceptance_criteria: Validate the observed immutable definition revision and select through the caller-owned inclusive cutoff.
Recheck the recurrence prerequisite and every selected absent coordinate in one immediate transaction.
Persist the complete page or none on duplicate, stale, corruption, serialization, storage, or competing-write failure.

attempts.diagnostic: Recurrence-store integration tests failed because persist_due_occurrences_page did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added focused integration coverage for the acceptance contract before adding production behavior.

attempts.diagnostic: Added shared due selection and atomic multi-stream append with typed stale, duplicate, bounds, and corruption failures.
attempts.patch: Added shared due selection and atomic multi-stream append with typed stale, duplicate, bounds, and corruption failures.

attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit suggested an additional non-empty cutoff-truncated transaction case. The finding was non-blocking because due selection/cursor truncation and committed-page atomicity were already tested independently, but it preserved a concrete lesson to combine policy and transaction assertions when extending the suite.
attempts.patch: Reused one due-page projection helper and kept the event-log batch helper crate-private. Reran the complete repository quality gate after the exact implementation state was ready.

outcome.summary: The kernel records a caller-selected bounded due unit without partial-page provenance or hidden clock, cursor, identity, or execution policy.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0184-atomic-due-recurrence-persistence.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 185 records: 185 valid, 0 invalid

lessons: Repeated single-coordinate writes cannot provide page-level crash atomicity; all selected streams need one transaction.
The immutable recurrence prerequisite and selected stream absence must be rechecked inside the write transaction.
Existing provenance should fail explicitly rather than become implicit sparse idempotency.
Combined cutoff-truncation and commit tests are valuable future defense even when each contract is already proven independently.
Atomic persistence records provenance only and grants no materialization, dispatch, retry, permission, or execution authority.
